solutionSql:
SELECT origin_id,
       COALESCE(SUM(distance_km) FILTER (WHERE destination_id = 1), 0)::integer AS km_to_warehouse_1,
       COALESCE(SUM(distance_km) FILTER (WHERE destination_id = 2), 0)::integer AS km_to_warehouse_2
FROM routes
GROUP BY origin_id
ORDER BY origin_id;

ambiguities.phrase: For each warehouse that is the origin of at least one route
ambiguities.readingChosen: Every distinct routes.origin_id appears, including origins with no route to warehouse 1 or 2 (shown as 0, 0).
ambiguities.alternativeReading: Only origins with at least one route to warehouse 1 or warehouse 2 appear.

ambiguities.readingChosen: SUM(distance_km) is cast to integer to match the stated column type.
ambiguities.alternativeReading: Leave SUM as bigint; values are identical, only the type differs.

notes: Conditional aggregation with SUM ... FILTER (WHERE destination_id = n), COALESCE to 0, grouped by routes.origin_id. Duplicate routes between the same pair are summed (sample origin 1 has two routes to warehouse 2: 125 + 108 = 233). A self-route to warehouse 1 or 2, if present in hidden data, is counted.
